newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BORSODCHEM MULLS MDI CAPACITY INCREASE-CEO.
newsitem.headline: BORSODCHEM MULLS MDI CAPACITY INCREASE-CEO.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt is considering to increase the output of its MDI plant to some 40,000 tonnes per year from 32,500 tonnes per year, Borsodchem's CEO said on Monday.
"We are seriously considering the plan and could start the investment this year," Laszlo Kovacs told a news conference on Monday.
Although its output volume is much smaller than that of Borsodchem's other main product, PVC, MDI (methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) last year accounted for 40 percent of the company's profits.
Kovacs said MDI hedges the company against the PVC price cycle, that last year resulted in reduced profits.

The average international market price of Borsodchem's main product, PVC powder, dropped 28 percent in 1996 from 1995, while main raw material ethylene prices only decreased 7.8 percent over the same period.
MDI prices, however, rose by an average 0.12 German marks per kg for raw MDI and by 0.33 marks per kg for pure MDI.
Borsodchem last year increased its MDI capacity to 32,500 tonnes per year from 25,000 tonnes per year, with an investment of 1.3 billion forints.
The upgrade was carried out by Japan's Mitsui which also licensed the technology to Borsodchem.
An analyst said if Borsodchem does go through with its upgrade plan, that is likely to benefit the company.
"Provided the feedstock for MDI is assured and depending on the licence fee (charged by Mitsui), it could be good news," Spencer Jakab, CS First Boston's Budapest-based analyst, told Reuters.
"MDI demand is seen increasing six to seven percent per year in volume terms."
Borsodchem is Central Europe's only MDI producer.
Borsodchem announced last week it had a net profit of 5.80 billion forints on net sales of 43.65 billion forints in 1996 versus 6.09 billion forints net profit on net sales of 41.34 billion in 1995.
The figures are calculated according to Hungarian accounting standards and are unaudited.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Borsodchem shares closed at 6,350 forints, up 310 on Monday.
